reviewedFrom: B12.1 and B12.2 definitions of done (advisor-plans/013), docs/books-revenue-recognition.md (expected loss and impairment).

contract-loss-lifecycle.derivation: A $100,000 fixed-price contract. June: $40,000 cost against a $110,000 estimate, a $10,000 expected loss; cost-to-cost earns 100,000×40/110 = $36,363.64, so $3,636.36 of the loss is already in the margin and the reserve is $6,363.64. July: $70,000 cost, estimate $115,000 (loss $15,000); earned $60,869.57, incurred loss $9,130.43, reserve $5,869.57. August recovers to $108,000 (loss $8,000) at $80,000 cost: earned $74,074.07, incurred $5,925.93, reserve $2,074.07 — only the excess is released. September completes at $108,000: earned $100,000, the full $8,000 is in the margin, the reserve is zero. Re-closing September posts no further provision.

contracts-not-netted.derivation: Contract A ($100,000, estimate $80,000) is profitable; contract B ($50,000, estimate $60,000) loses $10,000. B has earned 50,000×30/60 = $25,000 against $30,000 cost, so $5,000 of its loss is in the margin and its reserve is $5,000. A carries no reserve. Taken together the job forecasts a $10,000 profit — netting would have hidden B's loss.

home-impairment.derivation: Lot 3 carries $60,000 land and $200,000 construction, plus a $5,000 grading bill entered after a first review was prepared — that review is refused as stale and rejected. The current review: cost $265,000, expected price $250,000, nothing to complete, $10,000 to sell: net realizable value $240,000, write-down $25,000 (Dr 5070 / Cr 1170), approved by a second member. A later outlook of $260,000 (value $250,000 against the new $240,000 cost) writes nothing back. June and July close with the write-down tied to its review. Sold in August for $260,000: cost of sales by component is land $60,000, construction $205,000 and the write-down −$25,000, so cost of sales $240,000 plus the $25,000 write-down is exactly the $265,000 the home cost.

expected.staleApproval: refused: cost changed since the review was prepared
expected.selfApproval: refused: approved by someone other than the preparer
expected.recovery: refused: value covers cost, nothing is written back
